- 4h4.3's own description — full function-by-function contract + the returned signature shape {key,req,title,kind,sev,count,txCount,sourceCount,first,last,examplePointer}.

## Recently-decided context

Facts established THIS session that engine.js (a prototype) does NOT reflect — a verbatim port will be subtly wrong on all three:

1. **The emitted tx.* code set is a SUPERSET of engine.js's 7-entry CODE_TITLE.** 4h4.1 + the nfp fix landed 14 codes total. engine.js CODE_TITLE only covers 7: tx.missing_charset, tx.body_too_large, tx.parse_failed, tx.duplicate_transfer, tx.outdated_schema, tx.bad_media_type, tx.double_encoded. The 7 NOT in the prototype map: tx.unsupported_encoding, tx.undecodable_body (encoding.ts), tx.missing_schema_version, tx.unsupported_schema_version, tx.schema_invalid (schema.ts), tx.irregular_interval (interval.ts §3.4), tx.concurrent_delivery (concurrency.ts §2.1). EXTEND CODE_TITLE to cover all 14 with sensible labels — otherwise those 7 fall through to the raw detail string (functionally OK, never dropped, but verbose drift-prone titles, which is what signatures exist to avoid). Note: auth §1.3 fail (auth.ts:113) has NO code by design (auth path is out of scope of the code-wiring); it falls to the req+detail fallback — that is acceptable, do not add an auth code here.

2. **Field-name adaptation: the real FindingView is NOT the prototype shape.** engine.js uses f.sev and f.req; the landed view (src/api/sessions.ts toFindingView / src/web/api.ts FindingView) uses **f.severity** and **f.requirement**. The structured fields ARE already camelCase on the view: keyword, instancePath, param, code, plus outdated, detail, pointer. So sigKey/isIssue/sigTitle must read f.severity/f.requirement (+ camelCase structured fields), not f.sev/f.req.

3. **Real inputs replace the prototype's synthetic ones.** Findings come from the per-tx view (TransmissionView.findings: FindingView[]). The source Set for sourceCount keys off **tx.source** (raw transfer_src from 4h4.2; empty string '' is the single stable unknown bucket — keep it as a key, it counts as one source). Timestamps first/last come from **tx.received_at** (ISO string), NOT the prototype's minutes-since-midnight — compare as Date/epoch and emit ISO (or epoch ms) consistently. Keep the FOLD logic identical to engine.js; only the field accessors change.

1. **Single subagent — Signature engine (4h4.3)**
   - Reads: design_handoff_scale_at_volume/redesign/engine.js (port target), src/web/api.ts (FindingView + TransmissionView field names), src/api/sessions.ts toFindingView (confirm the exact emitted finding fields), src/api/source.ts (how source is derived, for the source Set).

Run order: serial, ONE agent. Pure module, no file sharing with anything else — but keep it solo since it is small and tightly specified.

- Wiring signatures into an endpoint — that is 4h4.4 (scope-aware summary), which this BLOCKS.
- The paginated/filterable list endpoint (4h4.5) — also blocked on this; txMatchesSig is built here but consumed there.
- Trend buckets / sparkline data (4h4.10 / scorecard).
- Do NOT touch the stages, repository, or sessions.ts beyond READING them for field names — this is a new pure module only.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit locally to this repo (no remote configured — do NOT push) when tested + green. One commit.
- Gates before commit: `npm test`, `npm run typecheck:web`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `npm run lint`.
- Terse commit style `<imperative summary> (4h4.3)` (run `git log --oneline` first).
- Close 4h4.3 with `bd close cce-data-delivery-validator-4h4.3 --reason="<sha> …"` when it lands.

title: Signature normalization engine (computeSignatures/sigKey/sigTitle)
description:
Implement signature normalization server-side: the pure projection of validator output that collapses identical defects into distinct "issues". Port the reference algorithm from design_handoff_scale_at_volume/redesign/engine.js VERBATIM in behavior (it is the authoritative spec).

WHY: One requirement (esp. §3.2 schema validation) can fail for many unrelated reasons. A requirement-level count cannot answer "what are the distinct things to fix, and how widespread is each?". Signatures can — and because they key off structured fields, they are comprehensive on day one with no catalogue to maintain.

WHAT: A new module (e.g. src/api/signatures.ts), pure (no DB/HTTP), unit-tested. Port these functions exactly:

- `generalizePath(p)` → strip array indices: `(p||'').replace(/\/\d+/g,'/*')` so /data/0/ABST and /data/7/ABST collapse to /data/*/ABST.
- `isIssue(f)` → true if sev==='fail', OR sev==='info' && outdated (outdated schema is a soft issue worth surfacing). Everything else (passes, plain info) is not grouped.
- `sigKey(f)`:
  - if f.keyword: `req + '|' + keyword + '|' + generalizePath(instancePath) + '|' + (param||'')`
  - else if f.code: `req + '|' + code`
  - else: `req + '|' + (detail||'')`  (last-resort fallback)
- `sigTitle(f)` → the only hand-written table (~1 row per Ajv keyword + per check code). Schema keywords: required→"Missing required property {param}", format→"{field} must match format {param}", additionalProperties→"Unexpected property {param}", type→"{field} has the wrong type", enum→"{field} is not an allowed value", minimum/maximum→"{field} out of allowed range", default→detail or "{keyword} at {path}". `field` = last segment of generalizePath(instancePath) or 'document'. Non-schema: CODE_TITLE[f.code] || detail || req, where CODE_TITLE maps each tx.* code to a label (copy the map from engine.js: tx.missing_charset, tx.body_too_large, tx.parse_failed, tx.duplicate_transfer, tx.outdated_schema, tx.bad_media_type, tx.double_encoded). Worst case for an untemplated edge is a plainer title — never a dropped or misfiled issue.
- `computeSignatures(transmissions)` → fold every issue finding into a Map keyed by sigKey, accumulating per signature: `count` (raw findings), `txCount` (DISTINCT transmissions), `sources` (Set of source ids → emit sourceCount), `first`/`last` timestamps, a representative `example` finding, and `pointer`/`examplePointer`. Sort by count DESC. (See the exact fold in engine.js computeSignatures.)
- `signaturesForReq(sigs, reqId)` → filter to one requirement.
- `txMatchesSig(tx, key)` → tx.findings.some(f => isIssue(f) && sigKey(f) === key). Needed by the list cross-filter.

Returned/aggregated signature shape (pre-aggregated for the wire — the browser must NEVER need every raw finding to render the summary): `{ key, req, title, kind: 'schema'|'check', sev, count, txCount, sourceCount, first, last, examplePointer }`.

TWO RULES TO HOLD THE LINE ON (confirmed with the team): (1) generalize the path, drop the value — strip array indices, never put the offending value in the key; ~3 normalization rules total, not per-failure logic. (2) Sign on Ajv's structured fields, not its message string.

INPUT NOTE: in the real app the finding rows come from the DB (structured fields from the structured-findings issue), and timestamps come from the transmission's received_at — not the prototype's minutes-since-midnight. Adapt `first`/`last` accordingly (epoch ms or ISO) but keep the fold logic identical.

OUT OF SCOPE: wiring into an endpoint (separate scope-aware-summary issue) and the trend/sparkline.
acceptance_criteria: pure signatures module ports generalizePath/isIssue/sigKey/sigTitle/computeSignatures/signaturesForReq/txMatchesSig per engine.js; keys off structured fields not message; array indices generalized, value never in key; computeSignatures returns pre-aggregated {key,req,title,kind,sev,count,txCount,sourceCount,first,last,examplePointer} sorted by count DESC; unit tests cover schema + check + outdated-info + collapse cases.
close_reason: aa3ed03 Add signature normalization engine — pure src/api/signatures.ts (+test), all 7 functions ported, 14 CODE_TITLE codes, gates green, clean review

title: Structured finding fields (keyword/instancePath/param/code)
description:
Persist and emit STRUCTURED fields on findings so signatures can be derived robustly. This is the foundation of the whole signature feature: without these fields, signatures can only key off the English message string, which drifts across Ajv versions.

WHY: A signature collapses identical defects into one issue. Its stable key is built from structured fields, never the message (README "Signature normalization", rule 2). Today findings carry only requirement/severity/detail/pointer/outdated.

WHAT (backend, no web layer here):

1. DB migration (db/initdb/30-finding.sql): add nullable columns to `finding`:
   - `keyword text` — Ajv keyword (the defect CLASS: required/format/additionalProperties/type/enum/minimum/maximum/…). NULL for non-schema findings.
   - `instance_path text` — Ajv instancePath (e.g. /data/0/ABST). NULL when not schema.
   - `param text` — the identifying param (missingProperty / format / additionalProperty / enum-of / …) — NOT the offending value. NULL when n/a.
   - `code text` — stable check code for transport/heuristic findings (e.g. tx.missing_charset). NULL for schema findings.
   All nullable, no CHECK churn. Keep existing `outdated` boolean.

2. repository.ts: extend `InsertFindingInput` and `FindingRow` with `keyword?`, `instancePath?`, `param?`, `code?` (camelCase on input, snake_case row). Thread through `insertFinding`, `insertFindings` (the multi-row VALUES builder — bump the per-row param count from 5 to 9 and add the columns), and the SELECT in `listFindingsForSession`.

3. Emit structured fields from the pipeline stages (the Finding type === InsertFindingInput, so stages just add fields):
   - schema.ts (Ajv): for each Ajv ErrorObject set `keyword: err.keyword`, `instancePath: err.instancePath`, and `param` = the identifying param pulled from err.params (missingProperty for `required`, format for `format`, additionalProperty for `additionalProperties`, allowedValues/enum for `enum`, limit for minimum/maximum, type for `type`). The missing/unsupported-schemaVersion fails and the outdated-info finding get `code: tx.outdated_schema` (info) etc. — see B-codes below.
   - Each transport/heuristic stage assigns a stable `code` at the point the finding is authored (NOT discovered in the wild — a finite, spec-bounded set):
     - parse.ts → tx.parse_failed (§1.1)
     - content-type.ts → tx.missing_charset / tx.bad_media_type (§1.2)
     - size.ts → tx.body_too_large (§1.4)
     - encoding.ts → tx.double_encoded (and any other §1.6 codes the stage already distinguishes)
     - semantic/duplicate.ts → tx.duplicate_transfer (§1.8)
     - schema.ts info → tx.outdated_schema (§3.2, outdated:true)
   Audit every `ctx.findings.push(...)` / `record(...)` across src/ingest/stages and give each fail/info finding a stable code (pass findings do not need one — signatures only group issues). The full code list is bounded by the spec's MUST clauses — known on day one.

OUT OF SCOPE: signature computation itself (separate issue), the API response shape, any web change.

NOTE: existing finding tests + sessions/compliance tests must keep passing; update fixtures (src/ingest/fixtures/transmissions.ts) and tests to assert the new fields where they already assert on findings.
acceptance_criteria: finding table has nullable keyword/instance_path/param/code columns; repository InsertFindingInput/FindingRow + insert/insertFindings/listFindingsForSession thread them; schema.ts emits Ajv keyword+instancePath+param per error; every transport/heuristic fail/info finding carries a stable tx.* code; tests+fixtures updated and green.
close_reason: aec5ac6 structured finding fields + per-stage codes; completed by 9d770a4 (nfp gap fix); every transport/heuristic fail/info finding now carries a stable tx.* code; all gates green

title: Scale-at-volume dashboard redesign
description:
Make the dashboard usable when one or many CCEs produce hundreds — eventually thousands — of transmissions. Follow-on to the first dashboard redesign (already shipped in src/web). Source spec: design_handoff_scale_at_volume/ (README.md is the authoritative narrative; redesign/engine.js is the authoritative algorithm for signatures + trend).

The first redesign assumed a handful of transmissions. Two failures appear as volume grows: (1) detail was appended at the bottom of the transmission list, forcing a scroll past everything to read findings; (2) each requirement rendered one chip per contributing transmission (180 failures → 180 chips). Both degrade linearly with volume.

The fix shifts the unit of attention from "every transmission" to scope + exceptions + summary, via four changes:
1. Docked master–detail pane — the list scrolls in its own region; the selected transmission's detail is pinned below it and never moves the list.
2. Scoped filter bar — a time window + source selector drive scorecard, compliance summary, trend, and list together.
3. Signature (issue) summaries — each requirement summarizes failures as a few distinct deduped issues with counts + source spread, not one chip per transmission. The load-bearing idea, with real backend implications.
4. Pass-rate trend sparkline in the scorecard.

The signature model is a PURE PROJECTION of validator output — not a hand-curated catalogue. Schema errors key off Ajv's closed keyword vocabulary; transport/heuristic checks key off a stable `code` assigned where the check is authored.

ALREADY DONE (carry-over from first handoff — no issue needed): delete-all-data endpoint, outdated-schema info finding on §3.2, 7-day retention.

NOT in scope (confirmed): status/severity filters in the filter bar; a global cross-requirement "Issues" rollup; "new vs recurring since last visit".

The prototype computes everything client-side because it holds the full finding set; at true scale we compute scope/summary/signatures/trend SERVER-SIDE and paginate the list. fleet.js is prototype-only and must NOT be ported.

This epic groups the backend (structured findings, source dimension, signature engine, scope-aware summary, paginated list, api types) and frontend (sparkline/icons, filter bar, dashboard scope state, scorecard sparkline, compliance signatures, docked master-detail, virtualization) work.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard stays usable at hundreds-to-thousands of transmissions: docked master-detail (list never reflows on selection); scoped filter bar (window+source) drives scorecard/summary/trend/list together; requirements show deduped signature issues not per-tx chips; pass-rate sparkline; signatures+scope+trend computed server-side; transmission list paginated+filterable+virtualized. fleet.js NOT ported.
close_reason: All 13 children landed + reviewed. Scale-at-volume redesign complete: docked master-detail, scoped filter bar, deduped signatures (not per-tx chips), pass-rate sparkline, server-side scope/signatures/trend, paginated+filterable+virtualized list. fleet.js not ported.

title: bat.1 fixtures break the typecheck/build gate (TS2352 in cloneValid)
description: src/ingest/fixtures/transmissions.ts:62 — cloneValid() casts structuredClone(validTransmission) directly to a mutable type: `return structuredClone(validTransmission) as { meta: Record<string,unknown>; data: Record<string,unknown>[] };`. Because validTransmission is `as const` (deeply readonly), tsc rejects the cast with TS2352 ('neither type sufficiently overlaps... convert to unknown first'). `npm run build` (tsc -p tsconfig.json) fails; only `npm test` (tsx, no full typecheck) is green, which is why it slipped through. This breaks bat.1's acceptance per cdd: 'Quality gates: npm test AND the typecheck/build gate.' Fix: cast via unknown — `as unknown as { meta: ...; data: ... }` — or drop `as const` from validTransmission. Introduced by commit 0673160 (bat.1).
close_reason: bed4c71: cast structuredClone via unknown; tsc -p tsconfig.json clean

- **The body is NOT auto-parsed.** `src/app.ts` calls `removeAllContentTypeParsers()` + a catch-all `parseAs:'buffer'`, so `request.body` is a raw `Buffer` and `request.rawBody` holds the exact wire bytes. **Stage 6 (parse) owns JSON.parse of those bytes** — there is no Fastify JSON parser to lean on. `rawBody.length` IS the §1.4 wire-byte measurement (measured AFTER content-encoding, i.e. the bytes on the wire — do not decompress before measuring size).
- **`buildApp()` is the factory; register the ingest route there** (or in a routes module it imports). Tests drive it with `app.inject({ method, url, headers, payload })` — no port needed. The registry is already on `app.schemaRegistry` (a `SchemaRegistry`); pass it to the schema stage via closure/decorator.
- **HTTPS scheme is `request.protocol`** (Fastify honors the scoped trustProxy + `X-Forwarded-Proto`; never blanket-trusted). Stage 1 reads that for §1.1. Note HTTPS is 🔒 enforced at the Caddy edge in prod — locally the header is absent so treat a missing/non-https scheme leniently (don't 400 on it); the real job of stage 1 is **method**: non-POST → 405. To return 405 (not Fastify's default 404), register the `/i/:uuid` handler for ALL methods and let stage 1 emit 405 for non-POST.
- **Schema registry lookup:** `registry.lookup(meta.schemaVersion)` → `{ok:true, entry}` (entry has `.validate` Ajv fn + `.sha256`) or `{ok:false, requested, supported}`. Unknown version → **422** with a finding listing `supported`. On a known version, run `entry.validate(body)`; on failure emit **one finding per `entry.validate.errors[]`** with the Ajv `instancePath` as the JSON Pointer → **422**. Store `schema_version` = the normalized key (use `normalizeVersion`).
- **Persist maps meta → columns** (only when parse succeeded; null otherwise): `transfer_id`←meta.transferId, `transfer_src`←meta.transferSrc, `transfer_type`←meta.transferType, `schema_version`←normalized meta.schemaVersion, `body`←parsed JSON (jsonb, null if unparsed), `raw_body`←size-bounded original bytes (kept ESPECIALLY when parse fails, for drill-down), `content_hash`←SHA-256 of rawBody (`createHash('sha256')`), `wire_bytes`←rawBody.length, `content_type`/`content_encoding`←headers, `http_status`←the final response code, `parse_ok`/`schema_ok`←booleans. **Record EVERY POST** — `insertTransmission` already has no ON CONFLICT; do not add one.
- **Repo functions you must ADD (thin, no business logic) to `src/db/repository.ts`:** `insertFinding(s)` (finding columns: transmission_id, requirement, severity∈{pass,fail,info}, detail, pointer) and a `bumpLastPostAt(uuid)` (or fold into stage 0). `createSession`/`getSession`/`insertTransmission` already exist; all take an optional `db: Queryable` so you can pass a checked-out client. **Persist the transmission + its findings in ONE transaction** (transmission first for its id, then findings) — use `getPool().connect()` + BEGIN/COMMIT and thread the client through the repo calls.

- **Stage numbering (avoid confusion):** DESIGN §6 numbers stages 0-8 where **stage 2 = Auth (M6, OUT OF SCOPE)** and **stage 8 = Semantic checks (M5, OUT OF SCOPE)**. M2 implements 0,1,3,4,5,6,7 + persist. Leave clean, documented insertion points (a comment / no-op slot) where stages 2 and 8 will go.
- **Success body** is a small JSON summary echoing the recorded findings count (a §6 teaching surface), e.g. `{ transmissionId, status, findings: <count> }`, returned with 200/202.

## Slicing recommendation

The stages share a `PipelineContext` and an ordered registry — so the framework agent freezes those first, then stage agents fill pre-created stub modules WITHOUT touching shared types/registry. Keep stage logic in per-stage files (e.g. `src/ingest/stages/<name>.ts`) so follow-on agents don't collide.

1. **Subagent A — 3bn.1 framework + 3bn.2 stage 0 + 3bn.3 stage 1 + 3bn.7 persist** (the vertical spine; runs first, serial).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6, §4.1, §8; `src/app.ts`, `src/db/repository.ts`, `db/initdb/30-finding.sql`.
   - Produces: `PipelineContext` type + `Stage`/`StageOutcome` contract (continue[+finding] vs short-circuit(status[,finding])); a `runPipeline` runner (collects findings, stops on short-circuit) with the §6 status-code mapping + success-body builder; the `POST /i/:uuid` route registered for ALL methods in/under `buildApp`; **stage 0** (session lookup → 404, bump last_post_at) and **stage 1** (method → 405, read `request.protocol`); the **terminal transactional persist** (insertTransmission + new `insertFinding(s)`, record every POST); the new repo functions. 2. **Subagent B — 3bn.4 (size/content-type/encoding) + 3bn.5 (JSON parse)** (after A; fills the body-bytes stub modules).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6 stages 3-6, §4.1; A's `PipelineContext`/`Stage` contract.
   - Produces: size stage (`rawBody.length` > 1MB → 413 + §1.4 finding); content-type stage (`application/json; charset=utf-8` check → finding, continue — 415 optional per §6); encoding stage (if `Content-Encoding: gzip` decompress with a **zip-bomb expansion guard**, detect illegal double-encoding e.g. base64 → 400 if undecodable, §1.6); parse stage (`JSON.parse(rawBody)` → 400 on failure, set `parse_ok`, ensure `raw_body` is retained for drill-down). Sets `ctx.parsedBody` on success.
   - Acceptance: unit tests via `app.inject` for each: 413 oversized, content-type finding+continue, gzip happy path, double-encoding 400, malformed-JSON 400 with raw_body persisted.

3. **Subagent C — 3bn.6 (schema validate)** (after A; fills the schema stub module; file-disjoint from B).
   - Reads: DESIGN.md §6 stage 7, §9; `src/schema-registry.ts`; the `meta` block of `docs/cce-interop-0.8.0.json`.
   - Produces: schema stage reading `ctx.parsedBody.meta.schemaVersion`, `registry.lookup(...)`; unknown version → 422 + finding listing `supported`; known version → `entry.validate(body)`, on failure one finding per Ajv error using `instancePath` as JSON Pointer → 422; set `schema_ok` + `schema_version`. A valid fixture transmission validates clean (you may craft a minimal valid 0.8.0 payload for the test).
   - Acceptance: 422 + supported-list on unknown version; 422 + per-error pointer findings on an invalid-but-parseable body; pass on a valid payload.

Do NOT build in this bite (each has its own epic):

- **Stage 2 — §1.3 auth enforcement** (M6, ct4.*). Leave an insertion point only.
- **Stage 8 — semantic checks**: duplicate detection (§1.8), interval regularity (§3.4), concurrency (§2.1), present-object inventory (§3.3) (M5, 8ji.*). Leave an insertion point only.
- **Sessions/dashboard HTTP API** — `POST /api/sessions`, `GET /api/sessions/{uuid}` (M3, 43b.*). The pipeline only *reads* sessions via the repo; tests mint sessions through `repository.createSession`, not over HTTP.
- Web UI (yih.*), retention worker (yhg.*), fixture-transmission test corpus (bat.1 — write just enough fixtures to test M2, not the full §8/polish corpus).
- Do not modify the vendored schema bytes or the M1 registry/trustProxy/raw-body wiring (it's correct; consume it).

- Gates green before each commit: `npm run build && npm test && npm run lint`. DB-dependent tests use the skip-guard from `src/db/repository.test.ts` so `npm test` stays green without Postgres; the persist + full-flow paths must ALSO be run live at least once against `docker compose up -d postgres` (paste the round-trip output in the agent report).

- src/api/source.ts — deriveSourceView: source key = TRIMMED transfer_src, null/blank → "" (UNKNOWN_SOURCE_KEY). This normalization is why a naive SQL `transfer_src = $source` is WRONG for the source filter (see below).
- src/db/repository.ts — listTransmissions (~255, the `(session_uuid, received_at DESC)` index + TransmissionRow shape) and listFindingsForSession (~279). Model the new query on these.
- src/api/sessions.ts — the 4h4.4 scope-aware GET handler (~184-322) just landed; mirror its param-parsing + view-building (deriveSourceView, toFindingView) for consistency.

## Recently-decided context

Facts established THIS session (4h4.4 landed at ac22588) that shape 4h4.5:

1. **scope.ts is the shared scope core — reuse it, do not re-derive.** parseWindow/parseSource already give resilient param parsing (unknown → default, never 400). title: Scope-aware session summary (window/source -> summary+rollup+signatures+trend)
description:
Make the session read endpoint SCOPE-AWARE: accept a time window + source and return the scoped summary + rollup + signatures + pass-rate trend buckets, all pre-aggregated. This is what lets every number above the list mean "within this scope" and stay meaningful at any volume.

WHY: At true scale the browser must not hold every raw finding to render the scorecard, compliance counts, sparkline, and signatures. The server computes them over the scoped set.

WHAT (src/api/sessions.ts, GET /api/sessions/:uuid — or a /summary sibling; choose and document):

1. Accept query params:
   - `window`: '15m' | '1h' | '6h' | 'all' (default 'all'). Define the scope as transmissions whose received_at falls in [now - window, now]; 'all' = no time bound.
   - `source`: a source key or 'all' (default 'all').

2. Over the SCOPED transmission set, compute and return:
   - `summary`: computeComplianceSummary over scoped finding counts (existing function — feed it scoped counts).
   - `rollup`: the gradeable passing/failing/untested rollup (currently computed client-side in Dashboard.tsx computeRollup / engine.js rollup) — move/share it server-side so scorecard numbers are scope-relative. Keep the exact spec (gradeable = verified|heuristic; failing folds mixed in).
   - `signatures`: computeSignatures over the scoped set (from the signature-engine issue), pre-aggregated, sorted by count DESC.
   - `trend`: pass-rate buckets via `passTrend(transmissions, 30)` ported from engine.js — 30 buckets across the scope's time span; each bucket `{ tot, fail, rate }` where rate = pass/(pass+fail) or null for empty; a tx "fails" if any finding sev==='fail'. Empty-bucket carry-forward is a RENDER concern (sparkline) — the endpoint returns raw per-bucket {tot,fail,rate}.
   - `sources`: window-aware per-source counts for the filter `<select>` (from the source-dimension issue): [{ source, sourceCode, sourceLabel, count }], computed over the window (NOT further narrowed by the selected source — the dropdown must show all sources' in-window counts).
   - `scoped` totals for the scope readout: total scoped tx, tx-with-failures count, distinct-issue count.

3. Keep existing behavior intact: 404 for unknown/expired uuid, session meta, expiresAt, the per-tx findings drill-down (still needed for the docked detail pane — but see the paginated-list issue for how the list itself is fetched). Decide cleanly whether the full transmission list still ships here or moves entirely to the list endpoint; document the split.

VALIDATION: reject/normalize unknown window/source values gracefully (fall back to defaults rather than 400, to keep the dashboard resilient).

DEPENDS ON: structured findings (for signatures), signature engine, source dimension.
OUT OF SCOPE: the paginated transmission list endpoint (separate issue) and all web rendering.
acceptance_criteria: GET /api/sessions/:uuid (or /summary) accepts window(15m|1h|6h|all,default all)+source(key|all,default all); returns scoped summary, server rollup, signatures (sorted), 30-bucket passTrend {tot,fail,rate}, window-aware sources counts, and scope totals {scoped,withFailures,distinctIssues}; unknown values fall back to defaults; 404/meta/expiresAt preserved; list/summary split documented.

title: NEXT BITE: M6 §1.3 auth opt-in (ct4.1-.3)
description:
## Underlying issues

- ct4: [epic] §1.3 auth opt-in (M6) — umbrella
- ct4.1: Credential generation + storage — dashboard generates token+header OR Basic creds; stored HASHED, plaintext shown once
- ct4.2: Stage 2 — enforce auth on ingest: when enabled, require correct credential else 401 (no row)
- ct4.3: Auth opt-in UI + config snippet — dashboard toggle → show generated credential + copy-paste config once

This is DESIGN §14 build-order step 6 (M6). M2 (ingest), M3 (sessions/dashboard API), M4 (web), M5 (semantic checks) are all landed. §1.3 is currently classed ✅(opt-in) in the §7 matrix and reads "Enforced once supplier enables the auth layer" — once this lands and a supplier opts in, the matrix grades 1.3 from real ingest traffic (render-only frontend for the matrix row; NO matrix changes).

## Read first

Memory:
- `bd memories` holds ONLY the M4 frontend-stack decision (React SPA + Vite + @fastify/static, src/web/ talks to the JSON API). Relevant to ct4.3's placement but nothing auth-specific. The §1.3 opt-in framing lives in auto-memory `architecture-decisions.md` and, more usefully, in the DESIGN sections below — reading those suffices.

Documents / code:
- DESIGN.md §3 (auth = "opt-in compliance layer, not a gate"; dashboard generates the credential), §6 stage table row 2 (Auth: "If enabled, expected token header or Basic Auth present & correct → 401"), §10 Setup ("toggle → service generates token + header name or Basic creds → shows config snippet"), §12 ("Auth secrets stored hashed, never echoed after first display"), §14.6.
- src/ingest/route.ts — the **Stage-2 auth INSERTION POINT** comment lives in `preBodyStages()` (after `sessionStage`, before the body stages); a halt here is 401 with NO transmission row (like 404/405). ct4.2 inserts the auth stage there.
- src/ingest/stages/session.ts — stage 0 idiom (injectable `db?`, `getSession`, `halt(404)`). The auth stage mirrors this. NOTE: session stage calls `bumpLastPostAt` on success, BEFORE the auth stage runs — see Recently-decided.
- src/db/repository.ts — `SessionRow` (carries `auth_enabled`, `auth_method`, `auth_header_name`, `auth_secret_hash`), `createSession` (already accepts `authEnabled/authMethod/authHeaderName/authSecretHash` but POST /api/sessions calls it with NO args → auth disabled). NO "enable/disable auth on existing session" helper exists — ct4.1 adds it. NEVER select/return `auth_secret_hash` to clients.
- src/api/sessions.ts — POST /api/sessions (no body, mints auth-disabled), GET /api/sessions/:uuid (already exposes only `auth_enabled`/`auth_method`, never the hash). ct4.1 adds the enable/disable-auth endpoint(s) here.
- src/web/components/Setup.tsx — has an explicit "auth opt-in toggle deferred to M6, NOT rendered here" scope note. ct4.3 removes that note and adds the toggle + credential display + config snippet. src/web/api.ts — the browser client (re-declares types verbatim; ct4.3 adds the new client fn + types here). src/web/routes/Dashboard.tsx — wires Setup's props / refetch.
- db/initdb/10-session.sql — the auth columns already exist (`auth_enabled` default false, `auth_method` CHECK in ('header','basic'), `auth_header_name`, `auth_secret_hash`). NO SQL change needed; verify only.
- src/schema-registry.ts:72 — the only existing hashing in the repo (`createHash('sha256')`). There is NO password-hashing dependency (no bcrypt/scrypt lib) — use node:crypto `scrypt` + `randomBytes` + `timingSafeEqual` (no new dep).

## Recently-decided context

- **No new dependency for hashing.** Use node:crypto `scryptSync`/`scrypt` with a per-secret random salt; store `salt:hash` (hex or base64) in `auth_secret_hash`; verify with `timingSafeEqual`. The §1.3 secret is the bearer token (header method) or the password (basic). sha256 (used for content hashing) is NOT appropriate for a credential — use a salted KDF.
- **Column mapping (internal to the new crypto/credential module — both store and verify go through it, so it is the single source of truth):** header method → `auth_header_name` = the configurable header name (e.g. `X-CCE-Token`), `auth_secret_hash` = KDF(token). basic method → `auth_header_name` = the Basic username, `auth_secret_hash` = KDF(password); verify decodes `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)`, checks `user === auth_header_name` AND KDF(pass) matches. This reuses the existing columns with no schema change.
- **Frozen export ct4.2 depends on (this bite's contract — analogous to M5's `SemanticCheck`):** ct4.1 creates `src/auth/credential.ts` exporting BOTH `generateCredential(method, opts)` (returns the plaintext to show once + the `{auth_method, auth_header_name, auth_secret_hash}` to persist) AND `verifyCredential(presented, session)` (returns boolean; `presented` carries the relevant request header value(s); `session` carries the stored auth fields). ct4.2's stage imports `verifyCredential` and does NOT re-implement hashing. ct4.1 OWNS and freezes these signatures before ct4.2/ct4.3 start.
- **Secret shown exactly once (§12):** the enable-auth endpoint returns the plaintext token/password in its response body; it is NEVER returned again. GET /api/sessions/:uuid must keep exposing only `auth_enabled`/`auth_method` (it already does — do not add the hash or plaintext).
- **Auth stage re-fetches the session** (injectable `db?`, like sessionStage) and reads its auth fields, rather than threading the session row through the pipeline — this keeps `src/ingest/pipeline.ts` UNTOUCHED (do NOT widen `PipelineContext`). The extra PK lookup is acceptable for v1 synthetic data. (Threading the row through both stages to avoid the double-fetch is a possible optimization but is OUT OF SCOPE here.)
- **`bumpLastPostAt` ordering wrinkle:** session stage (stage 0) bumps `last_post_at` on success, and runs BEFORE the auth stage (stage 2). So a request that 401s will still have bumped `last_post_at`. KEEP this behavior (do not touch session.ts) — a 401 still proves the session is live for the §11 retention clock; the row simply isn't persisted. Note it; don't fix it.
- **Auth stage no-ops when `auth_enabled = false`** → CONTINUE (zero-friction default; §3). Only when enabled does a missing/incorrect credential halt 401 with no row.
- **§1.3 is INGEST auth only.** Do NOT add auth to the dashboard read API (GET /api/sessions) — the capability URL is the dashboard's bearer authority (§3/§12). The toggle controls only the `/i/{uuid}` ingest path.

## Slicing recommendation

Mirror the M5 pattern: serializing Subagent A owns the shared credential contract + storage + API, then B and C run fully parallel against file-disjoint surfaces.

description:
## Underlying issues

- 8ji: [epic] Semantic checks (M5) — umbrella
- 8ji.1: Duplicate detection (§1.8) — flag repeated transferId + exact content_hash replays; never silently collapse
- 8ji.2: Interval regularity heuristic (§3.4) — ABST logger-timestamp regularity
- 8ji.3: Concurrency observation (§2.1) — in-memory in-flight request tracking per session
- 8ji.4: Present-object inventory (§3.3 info) — inventory which DS01 objects are present (informational)

This is DESIGN §14 build-order step 5 (M5), the FIRST semantic stage. It plugs into the existing ingest pipeline at the explicit Stage-8 insertion point. M2 (ingest core) and M3/M4 (API + web) are all landed; the §7 matrix already renders rows 1.8/2.1/3.4 (heuristic) and 3.3 (attestation) — once these findings land, the matrix flips AUTOMATICALLY (render-only frontend; NO web changes).

## Read first

Memory:
- The bd memory store (`bd memories`) currently holds ONLY the M4 frontend-stack decision — nothing M5-relevant, so do not chase it. The architecture context (capability-URL model, §1.3 auth opt-in [NOT this bite], the verifiability-spectrum framing the §7 matrix renders) lives in auto-memory `architecture-decisions.md` and, more usefully for a cold agent, in DESIGN §7/§8/§12 cited below — reading those suffices.

Documents / code:
- DESIGN.md §6 (pipeline stage table — stage 8 = semantic checks: 'findings; 2xx (data accepted)'), §7 (matrix classes/render rules for 1.8 🟡, 2.1 🟡, 3.4 🟡, 3.3 📝), §8 (data model + the (session_uuid,content_hash) & (session_uuid,transfer_id) dedup indexes; severity = pass|fail|info), §14.5.
- src/ingest/pipeline.ts — the FROZEN contract. PipelineContext is over-provisioned; stages read/write slots and DO NOT widen the type. Do NOT edit this file. Note `record(ctx, finding)`, `CONTINUE`, `Finding = InsertFindingInput`.
- src/ingest/route.ts — the Stage-8 INSERTION POINT comment lives in `bodyStages()` (after schemaStage, before persist). `persistTransmission` computes content_hash = sha256(ctx.rawBody). The handler builds ctx, runs pre-body then body stages, persists one row + findings.
- src/ingest/stages/*.ts — the one-file-per-stage pattern to mirror (schema.ts shows reading ctx.parsedBody/ctx.meta + emitting findings; size.ts/content-type.ts show pass/fail finding shape).
- src/db/repository.ts — listTransmissions, insertTransmission, insertFindings, FindingRow/Severity. NO 'find prior tx by transferId/hash' helper exists yet — A adds it.

## Recently-decided context

- **Stage 8 is body-side and NEVER halts.** Semantic checks always `record(...)`/return CONTINUE; the data is accepted (2xx). They run AFTER schema (stage 7).
- **Pre-populated context (confirmed):** schema stage (7) sets `ctx.meta.transferId/transferSrc/transferType/schemaVersion`; parse stage (6) sets `ctx.parsedBody`. So stage 8 reads transferId from `ctx.meta.transferId` and the payload from `ctx.parsedBody`. When parseOk!==true / schemaOk!==true, semantic checks should no-op gracefully (nothing to inspect).
- **content_hash for dup detection:** compute `createHash('sha256').update(ctx.rawBody).digest()` IN the duplicate check (route.ts computes its own copy at persist; do not try to share it across the frozen ctx). Query prior transmissions in the SAME session by transfer_id and by content_hash via a NEW repository helper.
- **Severity model drives the matrix:** heuristic rows (1.8/2.1/3.4) only leave 'untested' when a pass OR fail finding exists (deriveStatus in src/api/compliance-matrix.ts ignores `info`). So gradeable checks emit **pass when clean, fail when the heuristic trips** (per-transmission), with the 'can't judge justification' caveat in the finding `detail`. Inventory (3.3) is classed 📝 attestation → its status is ALWAYS 'self-attestation' regardless of counts, so 8ji.4 emits `info` findings that surface in drill-down only (never flips the row) — this is correct/honest, not a bug.
- **Concurrency (§2.1) is cross-cutting in-memory state**, NOT a pure per-request stage: it needs an in-flight counter incremented at handler entry and decremented in a finally, with the concurrent-count snapshot taken at entry. This touches route.ts (a shared file) → it lands with the serializing agent A, not a parallel stage.
- **§8 dedup indexes** ((session_uuid,content_hash), (session_uuid,transfer_id)) must exist in the first-boot SQL — A verifies/adds them.

## Slicing recommendation

Mirror the M4 pattern: a serializing Subagent A owns the shared files (route.ts wiring, repository.ts helper, the concurrency tracker + route.ts plumbing, the semantic.ts orchestrator + stub check files with a FROZEN check-function signature) AND lands the cross-cutting concurrency check. 1. **Subagent A — scaffold + concurrency (8ji.3)** — runs FIRST; serializes route.ts, repository.ts, the DB init SQL, and creates the shared stage + stubs.
   - Reads: pipeline.ts (frozen contract), route.ts (insertion point + persist), schema.ts (finding idiom), repository.ts, DESIGN §6/§7/§8.
   - Produces:
     - `src/ingest/stages/semantic.ts` — a single `semanticStage(deps)` wired into route.ts `bodyStages()` at the Stage-8 insertion point (after schemaStage). It composes four check functions and pushes their findings. Define + EXPORT a FROZEN check signature for B/C/D, e.g. `export type SemanticCheck = (ctx: PipelineContext, deps: SemanticDeps) => Finding[] | Promise<Finding[]>`, and create FOUR stub files A's orchestrator imports: `stages/semantic/duplicate.ts`, `interval.ts`, `concurrency.ts`, `inventory.ts` (concurrency A implements; the other three are stubs returning []).
     - Concurrency tracker: `src/ingest/concurrency-tracker.ts` (in-memory Map<sessionUuid, inflightCount>), with route.ts handler incrementing on entry and decrementing in a finally; capture the concurrent-count snapshot at entry and thread it to semanticStage as a dep (do NOT add a ctx field — ctx is frozen). Implement `concurrency.ts`: pass when the session was serial (snapshot ≤1), fail when ≥1 other request was in flight (§2.1 'serial delivery by default').
     - repository helper(s): e.g. `findPriorTransmissions(sessionUuid, {transferId, contentHash})` for the duplicate check; add the §8 indexes to the first-boot SQL if absent.
   - Acceptance: semanticStage runs after schema and never halts (2xx preserved); concurrency findings emitted under requirement 2.1 (pass/fail) with the tracker decremented even on throw; build+test+lint green; the three stub checks return [] so the pipeline is green before B/C/D land.

2. **Subagent B — duplicate detection (8ji.1)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/duplicate.ts` only.
   - Uses A's repository helper + `createHash('sha256').update(ctx.rawBody)` + `ctx.meta.transferId`. Emit requirement 1.8: **pass** when transferId+hash are novel in the session, **fail** when a repeat is observed (detail names which: same transferId vs exact content replay; note justification can't be judged). Never collapse.
   - Acceptance: a second POST with a repeated transferId (or identical body) yields a 1.8 fail finding on the new transmission; a novel one yields a 1.8 pass.

3. **Subagent C — interval regularity (8ji.2)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/interval.ts` only.
   - Reads ctx.parsedBody ABST objects' logger timestamps; heuristic regularity over intervals. Emit requirement 3.4: pass when regular, fail (or the heuristic's honest verdict) when irregular; no-op when <2 timestamps or unparsed.
   - Acceptance: a regular series → 3.4 pass; an irregular series → 3.4 fail; sparse/empty → no finding.

4. **Subagent D — present-object inventory (8ji.4)** — owns `src/ingest/stages/semantic/inventory.ts` only.
   - Reads ctx.parsedBody; emit requirement 3.3 **info** finding listing which DS01 object types are present (count per type). Informational only — does NOT grade (matrix keeps 3.3 'self-attestation').
   - Acceptance: a payload with N object types → one 3.3 info finding inventorying them; surfaces in transmission drill-down.

Run order: **A first** (owns route.ts, repository.ts, semantic.ts, tracker, stubs, init SQL), **then B ∥ C ∥ D fully parallel** (each owns exactly one file under stages/semantic/, file-disjoint; none touches route.ts/repository.ts/semantic.ts/each other). Each implementer adds unit tests in the node:test harness (pure check logic testable without a DB; duplicate's repository helper test may be DB-gated/skipped like existing DB tests; the concurrency tracker is in-memory → fully testable).

## Out of scope

- **Active-harness checks (§4 retry/backoff/Retry-After/abandon)** — deferred to a future milestone (DESIGN §15). NOT M5.
- **§5 guided retransmission** — deferred.
- **§1.3 auth opt-in (M6/ct4)** — there is a separate auth INSERTION POINT in route.ts preBodyStages; do NOT wire auth in this bite.
- **Frontend** — the §7 matrix + transmissions drill-down already render whatever findings land (render-only). Do NOT touch src/web.
- **pipeline.ts** — frozen; do NOT edit the context/stage contract. Do NOT change the persistence boundary.

## Commit + test expectations

- Commit to this repo (local-only; do NOT push — no remote). Terse `<prefix>: <summary> (<bd-ids>)` style; suggested prefix `ingest:` (matches recent semantic/pipeline commits).
- One commit per subagent: A `ingest: stage 8 scaffold + concurrency observation (8ji.3)`; B `ingest: duplicate detection (8ji.1)`; C `ingest: interval regularity heuristic (8ji.2)`; D `ingest: present-object inventory (8ji.4)`.
- Parallel B/C/D each `git add` ONLY their one check file + its test (do NOT `git add -A`); a beads pre-commit hook may re-stage .beads/issues.jsonl (expected). If git hits index.lock, wait briefly and retry once.

title: size: Fastify default bodyLimit (1MB) pre-empts the §1.4 size stage 413
description:
DESIGN.md §6 (lines ~89-90) says 'the app owns the §1.4 cap' so an oversized POST yields our teaching 413 + a recorded transmission row + a 1.4 finding. But app.ts builds Fastify WITHOUT setting bodyLimit, so Fastify's DEFAULT 1MB limit (== our cap) rejects any over-cap body FIRST with FST_ERR_CTP_BODY_TOO_LARGE: status 413 but body shape {statusCode,code,error,message} (not our {status,findings,transmissionId}) and NO transmission row / NO 1.4 finding persisted. Net: the §1.4 size stage's 413 path is unreachable end-to-end and the teaching finding is never recorded. Fix lives in app.ts (NOT a body stage): raise Fastify bodyLimit above 1MB (e.g. 1MB + headroom, or 2MB) so over-cap bodies REACH the size stage, which then emits the 1.4 finding and halts 413 with a persisted row. The size stage logic itself is correct (verified by a direct unit test at exactly 1_048_577 bytes). Discovered while landing the size stage (3bn.4).

## Context
Subagent B, M2 ingest body stages
close_reason: app.ts raises Fastify bodyLimit to 2 MiB (DEFAULT_BODY_LIMIT) above the §1.4 1MB grading cap, so oversized-but-bounded bodies reach the size stage → our 413 + 1.4 finding + persisted row; full-flow test added

title: persist: raw_body text column rejects NUL bytes from gzip/binary wire bodies (500)
description:
When a request arrives Content-Encoding: gzip (or any binary body), route.ts persistTransmission stores rawBody: ctx.rawBody.toString('utf8'). The compressed wire bytes contain 0x00 (NUL), which Postgres text columns reject: 'invalid byte sequence for encoding UTF8: 0x00'. The whole insert throws -> the ingest handler returns 500 instead of the stage's intended status (200 for a valid gzip happy path, 400 for an undecodable/double-encoded gzip). Repro: POST gzipSync(JSON) to /i/:uuid with content-encoding: gzip -> 500. Discovered while landing the encoding stage (3bn.4). Fix lives in the persist/repo layer (NOT a body stage): e.g. store raw_body as bytea, or store the size-bounded DECODED text when an encoding was applied, or strip/escape NULs. Coordinate with whoever owns route.ts/repository. The encoding+parse stages themselves are correct (verified by direct unit tests).

## Context
Subagent B, M2 ingest body stages

title: 404 handler: callNotFound() inside setNotFoundHandler degrades API 404s to plain text + logs warning
description:
When the web SPA build exists (production/docker image), buildApp() registers a custom setNotFoundHandler (src/app.ts:164-169). For a non-GET request, or any unmatched API path, it calls reply.callNotFound() FROM INSIDE the notFoundHandler. This is a Fastify anti-pattern: Fastify logs 'Trying to send a NotFound error inside a 404 handler. Sending basic 404 response.' (warn) and returns a degraded body.

REPRO (docker compose up):
  curl -i -XPOST -d '{}' http://localhost:3000/some-unknown-path
  curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/unknown
Both return: HTTP 404, Content-Type text/plain, body '404 Not Found' — and emit a warn log line each.

EXPECTED (per the code comment 'fall through to Fastify default 404/405'): Fastify's standard JSON 404, e.g. {"statusCode":404,"error":"Not Found","message":"Route POST:/some-unknown-path not found"}, and NO warning.

IMPACT: low. Every API/non-GET 404 returns a degraded plain-text body (broken API error contract) and adds warn-level log noise. Only manifests when webDist exists (SPA fallback registered) — i.e. the production image, not the no-web test path. Surfaced while driving the validator with the ems-data-simulator: posting to the wrong path (bare uuid instead of /i/<uuid>) hit this.

FIX: do not call reply.callNotFound() within the notFoundHandler. For the non-SPA branch, send the 404 directly, e.g. reply.code(404).send({statusCode:404,error:'Not Found',message:`Route ${request.method}:${request.url} not found`}) (or reply.callNotFound only via a separate, non-recursive path). Add a test asserting POST /unknown and GET /api/unknown return JSON 404 with no warning.
acceptance_criteria: POST to an unknown path and GET to an unknown /api path return Fastify's JSON 404 body (statusCode/error/message) with Content-Type application/json and emit no 'NotFound error inside a 404 handler' warning; GET /d/<uuid> still serves the SPA index.html.
close_reason: Fixed in src/app.ts: replaced reply.callNotFound() inside setNotFoundHandler (the re-entrant anti-pattern) with a direct Fastify-shaped JSON 404 ({statusCode,error,message}). Added regression tests in src/app.web.test.ts (POST /unknown and GET /api/unknown -> JSON 404, no SPA shell). Verified on rebuilt docker image: POST/GET unknown paths return application/json 404 with zero 'NotFound error inside a 404 handler' warnings; /d/:uuid still serves index.html. typecheck + lint + 8/8 web tests green.

title: Standard-revision proposals: schemaVersion identity, no-runtime-fetch, content-hash manifest
description:
Upstream suggestions for the next WHO-stewarded revision of the Interoperable CCE Data Delivery schema/standard. Not blocking v1 (our tool handles today's ambiguity via normalization — see DESIGN.md §9), but worth proposing since the standard is being revised.

Proposals:
1. Make meta.schemaVersion an explicit, opaque bare-semver token (e.g. "0.8.0") and state in prose it is an identifier the receiver maps to a schema via its own registry — decoupled from hosting. Drop the 'see the $id field' phrasing that conflates identifier with locator.
2. State that receivers MUST NOT dereference the schema at validation time and SHOULD validate against a pre-registered copy (availability, SSRF, and provability reasons).
3. Mechanically link $id and schemaVersion so there is exactly one version string and a deterministic way to derive one from the other.
4. Publish an out-of-band manifest with a content hash (sha256) per version, so any receiver can prove it holds the blessed bytes.
5. Fix the stale example: schemaVersion.examples is "0.1.1" (annotation-only, ignored by validators). Must be fixed upstream, NOT in our vendored copy, since we pin that file by content hash (DESIGN.md §9).

Context: DESIGN.md §9 (schema registry) and §15 (deferred).
